items.text: A new game called LangoPlay is changing how people learn English. It’s designed to teach you 3,000 words. The good news is that it’s completely free. How is LangoPlay different from other learning apps? It teaches you English through a story. You don’t need to memorize word lists or study grammar rules. With LangoPlay, you follow an adventurous story, and as you read and listen, you naturally learn new words. You can move at your own pace and take your time to understand each part of the story. The game teaches you words in the context of full sentences. After each chapter, you take a short quiz to test what you’ve learned. You also listen to the whole chapter, which helps you understand spoken English better. Each chapter takes about 20 minutes to complete, and there are 7 new words on average in each chapter. Complete 5 chapters a day and learn 35 new words. Learning a new language through a story works for all ages. Even people over 50 are finding success with it. LangoPlay isn’t just another app. It’s a new way to make learning a language enjoyable and effective. Are you ready to try something new and fun? Start your learning adventure today at www.langoplay.com . Are you good at marketing? LangoPlay is looking for a marketing specialist who wants to help promote the game. Difficult words: adventurous (full of adventure), pace (speed), quiz (a short test),.

A new game called LangoPlay helps people learn English. It teaches you 3,000 words. The good news is that it’s completely free. LangoPlay is different from other apps. It teaches English with a story. You don’t need to memorize word lists or study grammar rules. In LangoPlay, you read and listen to a story, and you learn new words naturally. LangoPlay is not just another app. It is a fun and useful way to learn English. If you are ready to try something fun and new, start your learning journey today at www.langoplay.com . If you are good at marketing, you can help us. LangoPlay needs a marketing specialist to help promote the game. Difficult words: memorize (learn words by repeating), quiz (a short test), just (only).

A new game for students is here. Its name is LangoPlay . It helps you learn English. You learn 3,000 English words. The game is free. LangoPlay is different from other apps. You learn English with a story. You don’t study grammar rules. You don’t memorize word lists . You read and listen. You try to understand a story. You learn new words naturally. After each chapter, you take a quiz. The quiz checks what you know. Then you listen to the story. One chapter takes about 20 minutes. Each chapter has 7 new words. If you play 5 chapters daily, you can learn 35 words each day. This game is for all ages . People over 50 can use it too. LangoPlay is a new way of learning. You can try it today. Start your learning at www.langoplay.com . If you are good at marketing, you can help us. LangoPlay needs a marketing specialist to help promote the game. Difficult words: memorize (learn words in your head), list (a group of words to learn), age (how old you are), promote (to give information about a new product).

Palestinians in Gaza say recent aid efforts are failing to reach most people. On Sunday, Israel and other nations dropped food packages and sent aid trucks into Gaza, but many residents say they received nothing. Israel has started daily 10-hour tactical pauses to allow humanitarian aid through; however, the UN and World Food Programme say these pauses are not enough. People fear collecting airdropped supplies because falling boxes have injured or killed civilians. Displaced families live in tents without food or clean water. Some say there is no real ceasefire , as bombings continue. Israel agreed to allow limited aid after global outrage over images of starving children. Israel claims Hamas steals aid to support its operations, but Hamas denies this. The UN says it has enough food for three months, but many people haven’t eaten for days and face famine -like conditions. The situation remains critical, with hunger worsening across the population. Difficult words: tactical (related to planned military actions), ceasefire (stop in fighting), famine (extreme lack of food). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People in Gaza say the food and help they are getting are not enough. On Sunday, Israel and other countries dropped food and sent trucks into Gaza, but many families got nothing. Israel now allows 10 hours each day for aid to enter, but the UN says this is not helping enough. People are afraid to go outside because food boxes fall from the sky and can hurt people. Many live in tents with no food or water. They also say there is still bombing, so they don’t feel safe. Israel says Hamas takes the food, but Hamas says that is not true. Some children are very thin and hungry. The UN says it has food ready, but many people still have nothing to eat. Life in Gaza is very hard, and people are asking for more help. Difficult words: aid (help or support), tent (small cloth shelter for living), thin (very slim). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Gaza say that they are not getting enough help. Israel and other countries send food and trucks , but many people have no food. Israel lets aid in for 10 hours each day. The UN says that it is not enough. Some people live in tents . They are scared. Boxes with food fall from planes and can hurt people. Many people are still hungry and afraid. They say that bombs keep falling, and they do not feel safe. Israel says that Hamas takes the food, but Hamas says that this is not true. Some children look very slim and weak . The UN says that it has food, but many people still do not get any. People in Gaza want more help quickly. Difficult words: truck (a big car), tent (a small cloth shelter for living), weak (not strong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Norfolk, the United States, police were surprised when they received reports of a man driving with a cow in his car, only to discover a massive Watusi bull as the passenger. This breed of African cattle is known for its gigantic horns. The driver, Lee Meyer, was stopped by the police, who issued him a warning due to the unusual and potentially unsafe situation. The bull named Howdy Doody could only fit in the car after modifications were made, including removing parts of the car’s body and windshield and installing a platform. The incident drew attention from onlookers, and it’s unclear where the bull and the driver were heading. Difficult words: breed (a particular type of animal or plant), modification (change), windshield (a window at the front of a car). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Norfolk, the United States, the police responded to reports of a man driving with a cow in his car. When they stopped the car, they were surprised to find a massive Watusi bull as the passenger. The police issued the driver a warning due to the unusual situation, which could possibly cause an accident. The bull’s name was Howdy Doody, and the driver had to make some changes in his car to fit the bull in. This incident attracted attention from onlookers who called the police. It’s unclear where the bull and the driver were going. Difficult words: massive (very big), attention (when people are interested in something), onlooker (a person who sees something happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Something crazy happens in Norfolk, the United States. People see a big bull in the back of a car. The driver’s name is Lee Meyer. He makes some changes to his car. The bull fits in the car thanks to the changes. People, who see the car, call the police. The police stop the car. The bull is a big Watsui bull. This bull has really big horns . The police explain the driver that the situation is dangerous. An accident may happen. The bull’s name is Howdy Doody. Reports do not say where the man and the bull are going. Difficult words: fit (to be small enough to stay in a place), horn (a hard part on an animal’s head), explain (to make something clear). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Airport security in the EU might soon allow travelers to carry bottles of liquid larger than 100ml in their hand baggage. This change is possible thanks to new screening technology that can detect dangerous materials even inside large liquid containers. These new machines have already been installed in some airports, such as Rome and Milan, but have not been used yet because they were waiting for final approval from the European Civil Aviation Conference. The European Commission has now confirmed that approval was given in June 2025, so airports that install the approved equipment will be allowed to use it soon. However, not all airports are ready yet, and some may need more time to buy and install the expensive machines. This fact means that while the 100ml rule may disappear in some places very soon, passengers should still check the rules at their specific airport before flying. The goal is to make travel easier and safer across the European Union with the help of better technology. Difficult words: detect (to find or see something that is hidden or hard to notice), specific (exact or special, not general). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Some airports in Europe will soon allow people to bring bigger bottles in their hand luggage . Today, people can only bring bottles with 100ml or less. The change is possible because new machines can now check what is inside large bottles. Rome and Milan airports already have these machines, but they couldn’t use them before. Now, Europe says that the machines are good and can be used soon. Some airports in Germany, Sweden, and other places will also get the machines, but not all airports have them yet. These machines are expensive, and it takes time to set them up . Therefore, the 100ml rule may still be in place at many airports for a while. Difficult words: hand luggage (a small bag you take with you on the plane), set up (to prepare or install something so it is ready for use), in place (already working or to be used). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Europe, people can only take small bottles when they fly. The bottles must be 100ml or less. Soon, this rule may change. New machines can check big bottles. Some airports have the new machines, but they do not use them yet. Now, the EU says that the machines are good. So airports can use them soon. Rome and Milan already have them. Other places like Germany and Sweden may get them too. But not all airports have the machines now. So people must still use small bottles in many places. The rule will change step by step . Difficult words: rule (something you must do), airport (a place where planes come and go), step by step (slowly, one small part at a time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chinese companies that produce children’s products are diversifying their offerings to include adult and pet clothing, as the country faces a record-low birth rate that is expected to continue declining. The demographic decline can be traced back to China’s one-child policy, which lasted from 1980 to 2015. While the limit has been raised to three children in 2021, couples are still reluctant to have babies. Yan Zhang, founder and CEO of Shanghai children’s clothing brand NATUNAKIDS, said the company’s sales have not been significantly impacted by the low birth rate yet but he expects sales to decrease over the next three to five years. The shift in the industry has left some consumers worried about their favorite brands going bankrupt. Market analyst Shaun Rein warns that companies in the baby industry will face declining margins , bad revenues , and falling stock prices. Difficult words: reluctant (unwilling to do something), margin (profit), revenue (income). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chinese companies that make products for children are expanding their product lines to include adult and pet clothing. The country’s falling birth rate is a result of the one-child policy that lasted from 1980 to 2015. The government raised the limit to three children in 2021, but couples are still not having babies. Yan Zhang, CEO of Shanghai children’s clothing brand NATUNAKIDS, expects sales to go down in the next three to five years. Customers worry that their favorite brands may go bankrupt as a result of the changes in the industry. Experts predict a bad future for baby companies in China. Difficult words: birth rate (how many children are born in a country in one year), brand (the name of products by one company), bankrupt (when a person or company has no money at all). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In China, fewer children are born every year. This starts in 1980 when the government says that people can only have one child. Now, companies which make things for kids are having problems. In 2021, the government says that families can have three children. But people do not want them. Companies start clothes for adults and pets instead of products for babies. Experts believe that sales of these companies will go down in the next few years. People who like certain brands worry that the companies will end. Experts say that baby companies will have a hard time in the future. Difficult words: pet (an animal which people keep at home, for example, a cat or dog), sale (how much a company sells), brand (the name for products of one company). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Eddie’s Sweet Shop in Forest Hills, New York, is celebrating its 100th anniversary this year. Known as the oldest ice cream parlor in the city, it offers a nostalgic experience for both locals and visitors. The shop has a vintage refrigerator over 80 years old, which still makes hand-whipped cream the traditional way. Many customers return with their families to enjoy the old-fashioned atmosphere and delicious ice cream. The menu includes a wide variety of flavors, from classic vanilla and chocolate to more unique options like rum raisin, coconut, and pistachio pineapple. Customers can also choose from various toppings, including butterscotch, hot fudge, and caramel. There are also classic syrups, such as cherry and root beer, that add to the nostalgic experience. Eddie’s Sweet Shop is known for its high-quality, homemade ice cream. Although the prices are a bit high and they only take cash, most visitors say the taste and charm make it worthwhile. It remains a favorite spot for ice cream lovers of all ages. Difficult words: parlor (a small shop or room where people get something special, like ice cream or a haircut), nostalgic (making you happily remember the past), vintage (old but special and good quality). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Eddie’s Sweet Shop is an old ice cream shop in Forest Hills, New York. It is 100 years old this year. Many people love to visit because it reminds them of the past. The shop still uses an 80-year-old fridge and makes fresh whipped cream. Some people visit the place with their children because they came there when they were young. The shop sells many ice cream flavors like vanilla, chocolate, coconut, and rum raisin. You can add tasty toppings like caramel, butterscotch, or hot fudge. The menu also has sweet syrups like cherry and lime. The ice cream is fresh and homemade. It costs more, and you can only pay with cash. But most people say it is a special place and worth a visit. Difficult words: flavor (the taste of food), topping (something you add on top of food), worth (when it is a good idea to spend money or time on something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Eddie’s Sweet Shop is in New York. It is 100 years old. Many people like it. It feels old and fun. They use an 80-year-old fridge. They also make fresh cream . You can get many ice cream flavors . Some are vanilla, chocolate, and coconut. You can add syrup like cherry or lime. You can put toppings like caramel and fudge. The ice cream is very good. It is not cheap. You can only use cash. Many people still go. They say it is a nice place. Difficult words: cream (thick white food from milk), flavor (the taste of food), syrup (sweet liquid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Coca-Cola plans to launch a new Coke made with cane sugar in the US this year. The company already uses cane sugar in some international products, but this would be the first widespread version in the American market. CEO James Quincey said the new version will complement existing drinks and respond to customer demand for natural sweeteners. However, switching from corn syrup to cane sugar will raise production costs and may affect supply chains. Despite falling sales volumes in North America and other markets, Coca-Cola beat profit expectations last quarter thanks to a 6% rise in prices. Volume dropped by 1%, partly due to economic pressure on lower-income consumers and a boycott in the US and Mexico. That boycott followed a viral video falsely claiming that Coca-Cola laid off Latino workers and reported them to immigration authorities. While Coca-Cola Zero Sugar grew 14% globally, analysts say profits were mainly driven by higher prices, not more products sold. The company expects strong earnings for the whole year. Difficult words: complement (to add to something in a positive way), boycott (when people stop buying or using something as a protest). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Coca-Cola wants to sell a new Coke with cane sugar in the US this year. The company already sells this kind of Coke in Mexico and some stores in the US. The CEO said it will be a good choice for people who want more natural drinks, but making it will also cost more. Last quarter, Coca-Cola made more money because it raised prices by 6%. Sales went down 1% because some people bought less. In the US and Mexico, some people also stopped buying after a video said Coca-Cola hurt Latino workers. But that video was not true. Coca-Cola Zero Sugar sold 14% more, but most of the money came from higher prices. The company still hopes for a good year. Difficult words: cane sugar (sugar which comes from a tropical plant called sugar cane), choice (what you choose), natural (without chemical substances). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Coca-Cola wants to make a new drink with cane sugar in the US. The drink is already in Mexico. People in the US ask for it. They want a more natural drink. The company says it is a good idea. But it is more expensive to make. Coca-Cola makes more money now. It puts prices up by 6%. But people buy a little less. Some people in the US and Mexico do not buy Coke. They see a bad video online about Coca-Cola workers. But the video is not real. Coca-Cola Zero Sugar is very popular . People buy 14% more. The company hopes this year will be good. Difficult words: cane sugar (sugar which comes from a plant called sugar cane), natural (without chemical substances), popular (when many people like something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ozzy Osbourne, the lead singer of the famous heavy metal band Black Sabbath, has died at the age of 76. Musicians and fans around the world are sharing tributes , including well-known artists like Ronnie Wood and Metallica. They are remembering him as a music legend and one of the most influential figures in rock history. In a video from 2017, Ozzy talked about the reasons why Black Sabbath ended. He explained that the decision was not easy, but he felt it was the right time to make a change. He also said the band never imagined that their music would inspire so many other groups and styles. Their sound became a key part of heavy metal music and helped shape the genre . Ozzy also reflected on the band’s beginnings. He said they started by playing in a small pub in Birmingham and had no idea they would become global stars. Their journey from local musicians to international fame surprised even them. Difficult words: tribute (words or actions showing respect or admiration), genre (a type or style of art or music). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ozzy Osbourne, the singer of the band Black Sabbath, died. He was 76 years old. Many famous people, like Ronnie Wood and Metallica, are saying nice things about him. They say he was a legend who changed music and helped make heavy metal popular. In a video from 2017, Ozzy said why the band stopped playing. He said it was the right time to end. He also said he was surprised that so many bands loved their music. The band started in a small pub in Birmingham, and they didn’t think they would become famous. But they became one of the biggest bands in the world. Many fans and musicians will remember him and his music for a long time. Difficult words: famous (when many people know someone), legend (a person who many people know or remember for doing something very well). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ozzy Osbourne is the singer in Black Sabbath. He dies at 76. Many people say thank you to him. They love his music. Big stars like Metallica or Ronnie Wood also say nice things. In one video, Ozzy talks about the band. He says why the band stops. He says it is time to stop. He feels happy that other bands love their music. Ozzy says they play music in a small pub in Birmingham. They do not think they will be big stars one day. But many people like them. Now they are famous in the world. Many people love Ozzy. Difficult words: star (a very famous person), pub (a place where people meet and drink beer), famous (when many people know someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many Canadians are now avoiding American goods in response to US tariffs and President Trump’s policies. Around 71% of Canadians say they are buying fewer American products. The ‘Buy Canada’ movement is growing, and it is hurting the US economy. Experts say the US could lose up to 90 billion dollars by 2025, with effects spreading to countries like Mexico and the European Union. Tourism is also affected. Canadian visits to the US have dropped by 50%, hurting border businesses. A Canadian grocery store owner says shoppers demand Canadian-made items and even avoid American brands like Coca-Cola unless labeled ‘Made in Canada.’ Some US food exports like wine and spirits have been pulled off Canadian shelves. Canada now puts a 25% tax on US alcohol. The boycott is spreading to Europe, where many now reject American companies. Tesla sales in Europe are down due to politics and brand damage. Global travel to the US is also falling, with visitor spending down by billions. The long-term impact may be a shift in global trade and a slowdown in economic growth. Difficult words: spirit (strong alcoholic drink), boycott (refusing to buy something as a protest), shift (a change in direction or focus). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many Canadians are angry at the US trade rules. Because of US tariffs and President Trump’s ideas, 71% of Canadians want to buy fewer US goods. Stores now sell more Canadian products. People even avoid US brands like Coca-Cola unless they are made in Canada. Canada now adds a 25% tax on American alcohol. Wine and beer from the US are disappearing from shelves. Visits from Canadians to the US dropped by 50%, which hurt US border towns. The US may lose 90 billion dollars in 2025. Europeans also don’t want US products. Tesla sales in Europe dropped 28% because people dislike the company’s boss, Elon Musk. US products are now less popular. Travel to the US from Europe is down, and the US will lose billions because of that. If these problems continue, American products may stay unpopular around the world. Difficult words: tariff (a tax on things from other countries), avoid (to keep away from or stop oneself from doing something), disappear (to be somewhere where nobody can see a person or thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Canada, many people are not buying American things. They are upset with the US rules and President Trump. A lot of shops sell more Canadian food and drinks now. People do not want US wine, beer, or other products . Canada puts a 25% tax on US alcohol. Fewer people from Canada are visiting the US. This is bad for shops near the border. Europe is also buying less from the US. Big US companies like Tesla and McDonald’s are losing customers . Fewer people from Europe are going to the US on vacation. Because of this, the US may lose 90 billion dollars this year. Difficult words: upset (unhappy and angry), product (a thing to buy or sell), customer (a person who buys something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In many countries, especially in Europe, local people are growing frustrated with the large number of tourists. In places like Barcelona and Mexico, protests have taken place, and in some cases, they have even turned violent. A big reason for this anger is that tourism has made cities crowded, raised housing costs, and put pressure on local resources, such as water, electricity, and waste systems. Cities like Barcelona now struggle to offer affordable housing as short-term rentals dominate the market. Some people also feel that tourism destroys community life. Local shops and homes are turning into souvenir stores and tourist rentals. Social media plays a big role, too. It sends thousands of people to the same locations just for one photo, which can cause chaos . Flights are cheaper now, so more people can travel, which adds to the problem. Still, many countries want more tourists. Places like Thailand, Vietnam, and Morocco depend on them. Governments are trying to balance economic needs with protecting local life. Difficult words: affordable (inexpensive), dominate (to take over or control something), chaos (a state of disorder and confusion). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In some countries like Spain and Mexico, people are angry about tourists. In Barcelona, locals used water guns on tourists. Protests happened in other places, too. Many visitors make cities full and busy. They also make rent more expensive. Some people cannot find a place to live because of tourist rentals . More tourists also use more water and power, and some cities don’t have enough. Shops change to gift stores, and local people feel like strangers in their own home. Social media and cheap flights bring more people to the same places just to take pictures. But not all countries feel this way. Thailand and Morocco still want more tourists. Some places now use tourist taxes or rules to help. People should try to travel in a way that is good for locals. Difficult words: rent (money you pay to live in a home), rental (a place you pay to live in), tourist tax (a small fee a tourist has to pay to some towns or cities). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people in Spain and other places are not happy with tourists. In Barcelona, they use water guns on them. Cities are full. Rents go up. People find it hard to live there. Tourists use water, power, and make waste . It is a problem. Social media makes some places popular. It shows one photo spot . Many people see it and go to the same place. It gets too busy. But some places like tourists. Thailand and Morocco want more. Some cities use new rules or taxes. We can help. We can walk, take buses, or have fewer showers. We can try not to make too much waste. We can think about local people when we travel. Difficult words: rent (money you pay to live in a home), waste (things we throw away), photo spot (a nice place where many people take photos). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Japan’s ruling coalition , led by Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba, lost its majority in the upper house of parliament during Sunday’s election. The result increases pressure on Ishiba, who already lost control of the lower house last year. However, he announced he won’t step down because of the urgent trade negotiations with the United States, which must be finalized by August 1 to avoid high tariffs on Japanese exports. Opposition parties gained seats, especially those promising tax cuts and more public spending. Voters were unhappy with the rising cost of living, particularly with food prices, such as rice. A new far-right party called Sanseito also gained attention and seats by promoting anti-immigration messages. The party started on YouTube but became more popular through its ‘Japanese First’ campaign. Experts say the ruling party will need to make compromises with the opposition, which could lead to more government spending. Foreign investors are now more uncertain about Japan’s economic direction and stability. Difficult words: coalition (a group of parties or people working together), promote (to support or actively encourage), compromise (an agreement where both sides give up something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Japan, Prime Minister Ishiba’s political group lost the upper house election. They didn’t get enough seats to keep control. Ishiba said he won’t quit because he wants to finish trade talks with the US before the August 1 deadline. These talks are important to stop new taxes on Japanese goods. Opposition parties won more seats. Many people voted for them because they asked for lower taxes and more help for families. A new party called Sanseito also did well. This group talked a lot about stopping immigration and said they want to protect Japanese people. Now the government must work with other parties to make new laws. This may lead to more spending, and some investors are worried about Japan’s plans. Difficult words: quit (to stop), trade talks (when countries talk together about business and money), investor (a person who puts money into something to make a profit). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Japan has an election . The prime minister is Mr. Ishiba. His party does not win. They do not have enough seats. But Mr. Ishiba wants to stay. He wants to talk to the US about money and business. The deadline is August 1. Other parties win more seats. People like their ideas. They want to pay less tax. They want more help from the government. A new party called Sanseito talks about stopping people from other countries. Some people like this. Now, Mr. Ishiba needs to talk to the other parties. They must work together. Some people who give money to Japan are not happy. They want to see good plans for the future. Difficult words: election (when people vote to choose someone for a political or official job), deadline (the last day to do something), party (a group of people in a government with similar ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At a zoo in northern Japan, authorities declared a twenty-four-year-old male chimp named Chacha missing after locals reported the primate roaming around their neighborhood. The animal was scaling power lines when dozens of workers and animal experts tried to coax the animal down using a cherry picker . That did not work, so the veterinarian shot Chacha with a tranquilizer gun. When the drug kicked in , the chimp fell down, and as he fell, he hit a lamp on the pole, which threw him off. He did not land in the nets and sheets that humans were holding below. Despite the seemingly painful fall, people reported that Chacha later made a full recovery. Difficult words: roam (move), scale (climb up or over), attempt (try), coax (make somebody do something), cherry picker (a thing often used by firefighters or builders which can move people up in the air safely), tranquillizer (a drug which makes you relax or sleep). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Northern Japan, a chimp escaped a zoo. The 24-year-old male climbed up power lines to try to get away. Workers and animal experts tried to use a cherry picker to get the animal down, but that did not work, so a veterinarian shot the chimp with a tranquilizer gun. After a moment, the chimp fell down. There were people on the ground who tried to catch him, but they failed. However, local media said that the chimp is fine. Difficult words: cherry picker (a thing often used by firefighters or builders that can safely move people up and down), veterinarian (an animal doctor), tranquilizer (a drug which makes you relax or sleep). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a chimp. It is in a zoo. The zoo is in Northern Japan. The chimp escapes . It goes to the city. It moves up in the power lines . People want to catch the chimp. It is not easy. They shoot it with a tranquilizer . The chimp falls asleep. It falls down. There are people on the ground. They try to catch the chimp. They don’t catch it. However, the chimp is fine. Difficult words: escape (to run away), power line (a cable which carries electricity), tranquilizer (a drug which makes you relax or sleep). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bed bugs are small insects that feed on human blood. They have been bothering humans for thousands of years. Out of about 100 species, only three feed on people. Bed bugs are hard to find and even harder to remove. They follow body heat, carbon dioxide, and smell to find people. When they bite, they inject chemicals that stop pain and make it easier to feed. Some people don’t react, but others get itchy, red bumps. Bed bugs hide in groups called refugia in small cracks or furniture where they stay safe and conserve energy. They can survive months without food and may go a year without feeding in cold areas. They usually stay close to where people sleep. People often bring them into homes accidentally via bags, clothes, or furniture. In the past, people used tricks like burning bed frames or using bean leaves to trap them. DDT almost wiped them out in the 1940s, but it was later banned for health reasons. Since the 2000s, they’ve returned and become more resistant to chemicals. Today, heat and vacuuming remain the best methods to fight them. Difficult words: refugium (a safe hiding place where bed bugs gather), conserve (to save or protect something from being lost or used up), wipe out (to destroy or remove something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Bed bugs are tiny insects that bite people and drink their blood. Only three types bite humans. They are very small and flat, so they can hide in beds, furniture, or walls. They come out at night and use heat and smell to find people. When bed bugs bite you, you don’t feel them, but they can cause red, itchy skin. Some people don’t feel anything. Bed bugs live together in small groups to stay warm and safe. They can go months without food and sometimes more than a year. People often bring them home without knowing, in bags or clothes. Many tried many tricks to stop them, like burning beds or using plants. A strong spray called DDT helped for a while, but it was later banned. Now, bed bugs are back and harder to kill. Heat and vacuuming still work well. Difficult words: itchy (when your skin feels uncomfortable and you want to scratch it), trick (a smart or simple way to solve a problem), vacuuming (using a machine to clean floors). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

One runner said the biggest challenge is staying balanced and avoiding obstacles as the ship rocks. Still, they are using this time to adjust to the freezing temperatures before the big race. The North Pole Marathon is known for its extreme conditions. Runners will face snow, ice, and freezing winds. One participant joked that they might even see a polar bear during the race, adding to the adventure. The athletes are excited and hopeful for a long, safe course to run. Despite the cold, their spirits are high, and they are determined to finish. Difficult words: obstacle (a thing in the way), spirit (a way of thinking, feeling, or behaving), determined (having decided to do something and not letting anyone stop you). In Emirates Hills, dubbed the Beverly Hills of Dubai, wealthy Indians are now outpacing China’s affluent in contributing to global wealth flows. The district attracts Indian businessmen with its opulent mansions, exemplified by a 2,400-square-meter villa belonging to the founder of Dano Group, a prominent real estate developer. Despite Dano’s establishment in the UAE three decades ago, the family’s increasing prosperity is largely fueled by wealth from India, with rich Indian citizens constituting a significant portion of the firm’s clientele. The UAE’s alluring combination of easy visa policies, low taxes, and geographical proximity positions it as the primary overseas beneficiary of India’s rising wealth, making it the anticipated top destination for migrating high-net-worth Indians. Difficult words: affluent (wealthy), opulent (luxurious), alluring (attractive or fascinating), beneficiary (a person or group that receives money or other benefits as a result of something else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A mysterious object from beyond our solar system may be the oldest comet ever found. Named 3I/Atlas, it was spotted last week by astronomers. Scientists from Oxford University believe it may be seven to eight billion years old, almost twice as old as Earth and the Sun. If true, that would make it the oldest comet ever recorded. This is only the third time an interstellar object has been seen entering our solar system. The discovery was presented at the Royal Astronomical Society meeting in Durham. The comet likely comes from the thick disc of the Milky Way, an area with many ancient stars. Later this year, 3I/Atlas could pass near the Sun and leave behind a glowing trail of dust visible from Earth. With new telescopes like the Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile starting powerful sky surveys, scientists hope to find many more of these rare space visitors. Difficult words: interstellar (coming from outside our solar system), ancient (very old), glowing (giving out steady light without flame). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Later this year, 3I/Atlas could pass near the Sun and leave a bright dust trail we can see from Earth. Difficult words: comet (a space object made of dust and ice), solar system (a Sun with its planets), trail (a line left behind). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Caster Semenya, a two-time Olympic gold medalist from South Africa, received a partial win in her legal battle against World Athletics. She has differences of sexual development (DSD), which cause higher testosterone levels. Because of this, she hasn’t been allowed to run in the 800m since 2019, when new rules were introduced to limit testosterone levels for some female runners. Semenya believes these rules are unfair and discriminate against athletes like her. The European Court of Human Rights said her right to a fair hearing was violated by the Swiss Federal Supreme Court during her 2020 appeal. However, the court didn’t decide if the rules themselves are discriminatory . Semenya’s case might now return to the Swiss courts. Although the ruling doesn’t allow her to compete again, Semenya sees it as a step forward. She wants to protect her dignity and the rights of others with similar conditions. Many people support her and believe she was treated unfairly. Difficult words: discriminate (to treat someone unfairly because of who they are), discriminatory (showing unfair treatment of someone because of their age, race, skin color, and so on), dignity (the feeling of being respected or valued). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Caster went to court because she thinks this rule is not fair. The European Court of Human Rights said a Swiss court didn’t give her a fair chance to speak. Caster cannot run again yet, but she is happy the court supported part of her case. She wants to protect her rights and help others like her. She fought for this for many years. Difficult words: condition (a health situation a person has), testosterone (a hormone in the body), support (to agree with someone or to help them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bosnia and Herzegovina is marking 30 years since the Srebrenica massacre. In July 1995, about 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys were killed by Bosnian Serb forces. This was the worst crime in Europe since World War II. The commemoration is held at the Srebrenica Memorial Center, which used to be a base and is now a museum showing exhibits and documents related to the genocide . Every year, newly identified victims are buried in the Potočari Cemetery. This year, seven more graves were prepared for this ceremony. Many people, including family members and other citizens, attend to remember the victims. Although the massacre is internationally recognized as genocide, some political leaders in the Republika Srpska entity of Bosnia and Serbia still deny that it happened. Some even glorify the people responsible for it. This continues to divide the country. Many Bosnians hope for unity and a better future. Experts say this will require more support from the European Union and changes to the country’s legal and political systems. Difficult words: commemoration (a ceremony to remember an important event), genocide (the killing of a large group of people because of their race, religion, or culture), glorify (to praise someone or something as being great, especially when it is wrong or harmful). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Some leaders in Bosnia and Serbia don’t accept that this was genocide . They also support the people who did the killings. Many Bosnians still want peace and hope for help from Europe to fix the situation. Difficult words: memorial (a place which helps people remember a person or event), massacre (killing a lot of people), genocide (killing many people because of how they look or what they believe in). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A fake Charlie Hebdo cover appeared online showing LGBT supporters in Moldova chasing away a priest. It falsely claimed Moldova had chosen a new religion and was shared widely on Telegram and social media. However, this image was not published by Charlie Hebdo. The real issue number 1716, published on 11 June, had a completely different cover about France’s interior minister. The fake image was meant to spread disinformation and attack Moldova’s Pride event. This is not the first time false Charlie Hebdo covers have been used for pro-Russian propaganda . Another example falsely described a peaceful anti-LGBT protest in Chișinău as a victim of police violence. However, fact-checkers confirmed the police acted fairly, and the anti-LGBT group tried to break through police lines. The EU’s disinformation watchdog reported that these stories are meant to promote homophobia and paint LGBT rights as against Christian or national values. In reality, many LGBT Europeans live with faith peacefully, and such attacks are based on false ideas. Difficult words: propaganda (information used to influence people’s opinions), fact-checker (a person or group that checks if news or stories are true), watchdog (a group that checks and reports on wrong actions), homophobia (fear, dislike, or hate toward people who are gay, lesbian, bisexual, or transgender). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The protest group tried to break police lines, and the police stopped them in a fair way. The EU team that checks false news said these stories try to make people hate LGBT rights. They use lies to say that Christian values are under attack. But many LGBT people believe in God and see no problem with Christian values. Difficult words: fake (not real), priest (a person who leads religious services and helps people in a church), in fact (a phrase which we use to show that something is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: cover (the front page of a magazine), religion (when many people believe in a god), priest (a person who works in a church), lie (something what is not true) You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Janet Dingwell found what looked like a World War II landmine on a beach in Red Head, Canada. She contacted the police, who waited for a special team from Gagetown to investigate. Janet’s suspicion came from a childhood experience. Her sister Julie recalled a time in the 1960s when they found a similar object on the same beach. As children, they rolled it home thinking it was a treasure. Their father quickly realized it was a mine and made them lie on the floor until help arrived. Jeff Allard, a technician at CFB Gagetown, says his team responds to 20–30 calls a year about unusual or dangerous items. Some are found when people clean out old houses, dig in their yards, or walk on beaches. Many of these objects are from past wars and are still dangerous. Allard’s team took Janet’s call seriously because of the area’s history. In the end, it was just an old propane tank buried in the sand with only the top showing. Difficult words: suspicion (a feeling that something is wrong), recall (to remember), propane (a flammable gas). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Janet remembered a story from her childhood . Her sister said they once found a big metal ball on the beach and took it home. Their dad was very scared because it was a real mine. He told them to lie down and wait. Jeff Allard works with a special team at CFB Gagetown. He says they get many calls every year about old bombs or other dangerous things. These things can be in fields, homes, or even cemeteries . In the end, Janet’s object was not a bomb. It was an old gas tank. Difficult words: landmine (a bomb under the ground), childhood (the time when you are a child), cemetery (a place where we bury dead people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
